General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ieee ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2957 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.
  • Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.
  • Last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

Last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Sources indicate that the tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully launched on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

Industry observers note that this mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

In a recent development, “I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” claims Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”.

Sources indicate that phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

According to recent reports, more than 10 years in the making, MMX rolled out on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a new rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA.

MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

If all goes according to plan, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images.

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” says Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images.

Once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to strategy, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” says Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

According to recent reports, from that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot.

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

The best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

According to recent reports, during its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

Before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu says, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA.

It will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

Industry observers note that idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR.

“It will bounce probably several times,” notes Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

Industry observers note that A simulation reveals how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR.

Once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” notes Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

The WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she states. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”.

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR.

The team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday states.

Despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday says Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy.

Recent findings suggest that idefix’s interactions with its latest home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec says. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”.

According to recent reports, what Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel indicates the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

According to recent reports, once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

The MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

Sources indicate that the coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel indicates. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”.

Probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA.

It has been revealed that the pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this glitch and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu claims.

According to recent reports, one of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

Industry observers note that that possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA.

During the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

According to recent reports, once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA.

Finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

“We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel says. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

According to recent reports, “MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu claims. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

Rosalía gushed that it was an “honor” for Taylor Swift to hail her Grammy-nominated Lux as a “perfect album” and said that she considers the pop star a “master songwriter.”.

“To me, she’s a master, honestly,” Rosalía remarked during a red carpet interview for the Los40 Music Awards in Barcelona on Friday. “I think she’s incredible.” The Spanish singer also revealed her favorite Swift track. “I prefer individual songs rather than albums,” she added. “There’s one I really love, “Wildest Dreams.” It’s one of the songs I’ve listened to the most in my entire life.”.

Swift had sung Rosalía’s praise earlier this month during a press conference for the nominations for the Golden Globes, which she is up for Best Original Song for the Toy Story 5 track, “I Knew It, I Knew You.”   Trending Stories Patrick Stewart Cause of Death Revealed Rosalía Calls Taylor Swift a 'Master Songwriter,' Reveals Her Favorite Swift Track ‘Yes, Dear’ Star Anthony Clark's Cause of Death Revealed Marlon Jackson Reveals Stage 4 Prostate Cancer Diagnosis.

According to recent reports, “Two perfect albums that I love and that I kept coming back to are from Olivia Dean and Rosalía,” Swift shared about what will likely end up on her Spotify Wrapped this year. “For Rosalía, she has created an ambitious and expansive concept album that could’ve only come from her vital life experience. Those albums are marvelous because they’re human, they’re made for people and are about the human experience; that’s why humans connect with them.”.

The women’s camaraderie and mutual respect comes ahead of the 2027 Grammys where both are going up against each other in several categories, including Album of the Year for Rosalía’s classically experiment Lux and Swift’s glitzy The Life of a Showgirl, as well as Record of the Year for “Berghain” and “The Fate of Ophelia.”.

One of the best headphone deals right now is for my favorite headphones: Sony's 1000X series has been around since 2016, with each new model improving on the previous iteration; the latest being the Sony WH-1000XM6, released in 2025. These are the best over-ear headphones I tested in 2025 (or ever, really). Right now, you can get the WH-1000XM6 headphones for $348 (originally $459.99), their lowest price ever during the early Black Friday sale from Amazon.

The XM6 headphones improve on what were already excellent headphones. Sony upped the count of microphones from eight to 12 when compared to the XM5, which improves more than just how well you sound to someone on a phone call. The microphones are used in almost all of its features, like ANC, Adaptive Sound Control, and the headphones' Ambient Sound mode. They hear your surroundings to adapt their features accordingly. If you switch from a noisy room to a quiet one, the XM6 can switch from ANC to "aware mode" (if you have Adaptive Sound Control on).

It has been revealed that these headphones have a lot more features that you can nerd out on in their companion app. The audio quality is second to none, with the fully customizable EQ giving you plenty of options to get the sound how you like it. I really like being able to see what codec you're listening to in the app's main menu. That way, there's no guessing if you're getting the best audio quality or not. They will give you 30 hours of battery life with ANC on and 40 hours of juice with ANC off. There's an AUX (3.5mm) jack for wired listening, which is a nice touch for audiophiles who still rock iPod Classics (or is that just me?).

Industry observers note that the XM6s were not just the best headphones of 2025, but are still the best ones of 2026 and likely to be the best ones for years to come. For $348, you'll be securing the best for a record-low price.

Anthony Clark’s cause of death has been revealed.

The Nineties stand-up comedian who starred in the long-running sitcom died on Nov. 10 at 63. His death certificate listed his cause of death as septic shock, with influenza A and chronic alcoholism noted as underlying conditions, People reported. Acute kidney failure was added as a significant contributing factor.

Clark’s Yes, Dear co-star Mike O’Malley shared news of the actor’s death on social media earlier this month. “When my wife Lisa and I were dating back in the mid-nineties, Anthony was already famous in Boston, regularly selling out comedy indicates. The first time we saw him at The Comedy Connection we laughed and laughed and laughed,” O’Malley, who starred alongside Clark for six seasons on the show, wrote in a post. “He was so unique — one of those comics who is laughing along with you at the absurdity of his stories and observations.” Trending Stories Patrick Stewart Cause of Death Revealed Rosalía Calls Taylor Swift a 'Master Songwriter,' Reveals Her Favorite Swift Track ‘Yes, Dear’ Star Anthony Clark's Cause of Death Revealed Marlon Jackson Reveals Stage 4 Prostate Cancer Diagnosis.

Clark portrayed Gregory Thomas “Greg” Warner in Yes, Dear, which chronicled two married couples figuring out parenthood. Clark’s tightly wound Greg comically contrasted to his wilder brother-in-law played by O’Malley. The show became a hit with audiences, enjoying six years on CBS from 2000 to 2006 and an even longer run in syndication.

It has been revealed that “I was a fan before I was a friend. We spoke on the phone three weeks ago. He had us laughing loudly once again,” mentioned O’Malley in his tribute, alongside photos from their last episode of Yes Dear after 122 total episodes. “Rest in peace. Tony.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I still haven't started my holiday shopping, but that's OK — I have plenty of movies to watch! As November stretches on, I need a great movie night now more than ever. Good thing Prime Video has loaded up its ever-tempting library this month, so rather than letting you burn half the evening scrolling, I’ve picked out three films I reckon will see you through the weekend in style on one of the best streaming services out there.

First up is a brand-fresh biopic that turns Nicolas Cage loose as John Madden, and he's weirdly perfect in the role. Then there’s a gloriously daft comic-book romp that bombed back in 1995 and has spent the decades building a devoted cult. And to round things off, I’ve gone for a cheesy, heartwarming Disney holiday comedy from peak Jonathan Taylor Thomas.

So cozy up with your blanket, raid the fridge for some snacks, and read on for three movies worth streaming on Prime Video this weekend.

In a recent development, I didn’t have “Nicolas Cage plays John Madden” on my 2026 bingo card, but here we are, and I’m thrilled about it, even though I don't much care for football. I care about games, and I care about Cage, and you get plenty of both here.

Recent findings suggest that “Madden” is a biopic of the Hall of Fame coach, broadcaster and game namesake, and Cage throws himself into the role with exactly the kind of energy you're probably hoping for. Director David O. Russell traces Madden’s whole arc, from his Super Bowl-winning years running the Oakland Raiders to the legendary broadcasting career that made him a household name, right up to the video game that slapped his name on millions of games for multiple consoles.

Whether you grew up quoting Madden’s broadcasts or just spent your weekends button-mashing through “Madden NFL,” this one’s a loving, larger-than-life tribute to an American original.

Watch "Madden" on Prime Video on Nov. 18.

If your nostalgia receptors are still calibrated to the late ’90s, “I’ll Be Home for Christmas” is going to hit you like a Mack truck. This 1998 Disney comedy is pure, uncut comfort food, starring peak-era Jonathan Taylor Thomas. He plays Jake, a spoiled college kid on the west coast whose estranged dad (Gary Cole) dangles a vintage Porsche in front of him if he can just make it home to Fresh York for Christmas.

Recent findings suggest that naturally, nothing goes as it should. Some classmates strand Jake out in the desert wearing a Santa suit and beard, and he has to figure out how to get home before the holiday clock runs out. Meanwhile, his girlfriend Allie (Jessica Biel) gives up waiting and accepts a cross-country ride from Jake’s rival.

In a recent development, look, it’s not reinventing the genre, and that's fine. But JTT is genuinely charming as a selfish kid who slowly figures out what the season’s actually about. Relax and let the holiday vibes wash over you.

Watch "I'll Be Home For Christmas" on Prime Video.

Some movies are good, some movies are bad, and some movies are “Tank Girl." This 1995 cult oddity flopped on release and then spent the next three decades becoming the kind of movie people force their friends to watch at 1 a.m. I am now one of those people, so consider this me pressing it on you.

Lori Petty is Rebecca Buck, aka Tank Girl, a punky blonde surviving in a post-apocalyptic 2033 where a nasty megacorporation called Water & Power is hoarding all the well, water and power. When Kesslee (Malcolm McDowell) kills her friends and burns down her life, Rebecca commandeers a tank, teams up Jet Girl (Naomi Watts) and a band of kangaroo-human mutant rebels called the Rippers, and sets out to bring the whole system down.

Recent findings suggest that adapted from the Jamie Hewlett and Alan Martin comic, years before Hewlett co-created Gorillaz, the movie is an explosion of punk attitude, comic-book panels, musical numbers, and anything-goes weirdness. It makes almost no sense and absolutely does not care, and that's absolutely why you should check it out. Yesterday.

Watch "Tank Girl" on Prime Video now.

Electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then demonstrates how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This repository holds the paper Finite-time blow-up for the Navier–Stokes equations by L.
  • The statement files at the top of lean/ give the definitions and state the theorems with sorry in place of their proofs; Solution.lean proves them from the library lean/Breakdown/.
  • The library is large (about 2,270 files and 600,000 lines), and a full build needs a great deal of memory and time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This repository holds the paper Finite-time blow-up for the Navier–Stokes equations by L. Alpöge and T. Buckmaster and the Lean 4 formalization that accompanies it.

The statement files at the top of lean/ give the definitions and state the theorems with sorry in place of their proofs; Solution.lean proves them from the library lean/Breakdown/. Each comparator*.json pairs a statement file with Solution.lean, names the theorems whose statements must agree, and permits only the axioms propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice.

The library is large (about 2,270 files and 600,000 lines), and a full build needs a great deal of memory and time.

Recent findings suggest that the formalization contains no data. The certificate whose hash the paper gives is not in this repository; the paper claims that it will be released. That the certificate satisfies the conditions of Appendix B is verified by a rigorous computation, involving interval arithmetic (128 bits of precision, with the Arb library through FLINT), which is not part of the formalization and is not in this repository either.

The source of the paper is not in this repository.

Recent findings suggest that the package is the one of the paper's working repository, with one patch of 20 November 2026 applied to the cell-layer statements and to the library proofs that depend on them: the weight of one bound becomes $(|m|+\tfrac12)^2$ in place of $m^2+\tfrac14$, one constant of a cell may be zero, and the set of the harmonics of the model in a cell is restricted to those that do not vanish there. Appendix B of the paper states the conditions in this patched form. The patched package was not rebuilt when this repository was assembled.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A jury found a former Los Angeles resident guilty of starting what became the deadly Palisades Fire of January 2025, the city’s most destructive wildfire in its history.

Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, was convicted of one count of destruction of property by means of fire and one count of arson affecting property used in interstate commerce. Federal prosecutors accused Rinderknecht of intentionally starting the original blaze, known as the Lachman fire. While the initial fire was swiftly suppressed, unbeknownst to firefighters and other authorities at the time, embers of it continued to burn underground. On Jan. 7, heavy winds reignited the fire, causing it to surface and spread. The ensuing Palisades fire was one of the most destructive wildfires in Los Angeles history, killing 12 people and decimating 23,448 acres of land and nearly 7,000 structures across the Pacific Palisades region.

According to recent reports, “Twelve people lost their lives and thousands lost their homes because of Jonathan Rinderknecht’s malicious conduct,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche in a statement. “Thanks to the persistence and hard work of our prosecutors in the Central District of California, he will be held accountable.”.

Sources indicate that “Jonathan Rinderknecht deliberately ignited a fire that killed 12 people and devastated an entire community,” stated First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli. “We were determined to hold him accountable, and today’s guilty verdict delivers a measure of justice for the families who lost loved ones and the thousands whose lives were upended.”.

After a federal jury in June deadlocked in favor of acquittal in Rinderknecht’s first trial in June, federal prosecutors narrowed their case to charge him with the two arson-related felonies rather than the three charges in the mistrial.

It has been revealed that steve Haney, the man’s lawyer for both trials, told the Los Angeles Times that they planned to appeal Friday’s verdict. “We are disappointed in the verdict, but respect the jury process,” Haney told the publication. “After a lengthy deliberation, they clearly gave this case a great deal of consideration.” Trending Stories Patrick Stewart Cause of Death Revealed Rosalía Calls Taylor Swift a 'Master Songwriter,' Reveals Her Favorite Swift Track ‘Yes, Dear’ Star Anthony Clark's Cause of Death Revealed Marlon Jackson Reveals Stage 4 Prostate Cancer Diagnosis Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

The prosecution argued that Rinderknecht, who was working on New Year’s Eve as an Uber driver on Dec. 31, 2024, was angry and frustrated because he was unable to find companionship on New Year’s. According to an affidavit from an investigator for the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, two of his passengers described him as “agitated and angry” that night. He allegedly drove to a Pacific Palisades trailhead, where he repeatedly listened to and watched a music video for the rap song, “Un Zder, Un Thé,” about despair, and tried calling an old friend, but was unable to connect with them.Prosecutors said that Rinderknecht started the Lachman Fire just after midnight, and that around 12:12 a.m. on Jan. 1, 2025, environmental sensing platforms indicated the Lachman fire had begun. They said that Rinderknecht called 911 several times, but didn’t get through because his iPhone was out of range. By the time he finally connected with the police, the fire had already been reported by others in the neighborhood.

During his call with police, per the affidavit, Rinderknecht also allegedly typed a question into ChatGPT: “Are you at fault if a fire is lift [sic] because of your cigarette?” ChatGPT allegedly responded “Yes.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is steeped with nostalgia for Hollywood’s past, David Fincher claims to represent the future.

While many have criticized the Quentin Tarantino-penned sequel to Once Upon a Time in Hollywood (2019) for the apparent onscreen use of Gen AI, the 3x Oscar-nominated director recently shared his thoughts on the rapidly growing tech.

“I’m not a Luddite, so I don’t fear the unknown,” Fincher told the Los Angeles Times.

Sources indicate that “Is everyone satisfied that we have figured this art form out enough that what we really need to do is go back to celluloid?” he continued. “How long have people painted? 40,000 years? We’re talking about a thing that’s a hundred years old and everyone’s going, ‘Stop. Pencils down. No more iterating. It’s not necessary to have at your fingertips the ability to change the color of that person’s eyes.'” Watch on Deadline.

According to recent reports, fincher added, “Well, it exists. Should we not use it?”.

The comments come as several fans have taken to social media to criticize the apparent use of AI in the film as “astounding to an absurd degree,” with one viewer saying they “walked out of Cliff Booth completely gutted.”.

Set in 1977, eight years after Once Upon a Time…, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth follows Brad Pitt’s eponymous stuntman, now a projectionist who moonlights as a Hollywood fixer, getting caught up in a conspiracy that involves a Filipino gang and a stolen Oscar.

It has been revealed that premiering Thanksgiving on Imax, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth premieres Dec. 23 on Netflix.

Type: Foam + Micro coilsDepth: 3"Cover: CottonCorner straps: YesTrial period: 45 nightsWarranty: 1-year warrantyStarting MSRP: from $235 at Saatva.

Industry observers note that the Saatva Micro-Coil Mattress Topper has a soft, contouring surface with an enough give around the shoulders and hips to make side sleeping the most comfortable position, with back sleeping a close second. In a recent development, as a back and stomach sleeper, the topper is almost too soft for my liking, but not enough to prevent a deep night’s sleep. But as long as I slept in lightweight pyjamas and breathable bedding, I was able to comfortably sleep through the night. If I wore anything heavier, I woke up to some warmth.

It has been revealed that ultimately, the Saatva Micro-Coil Topper is a great choice for anyone looking to soften up a too-firm mattress or prolong the life of a bed that's losing its support. Don't let the micro-coil layer fool you, it's softer than advertised. But if you're a side or back sleeper looking to sample the luxury of the best Saatva mattresses as a fraction of the cost, I highly recommend it.

Industry observers note that micro coils are the newest innovation for toppers so they’re often priced higher than expected. Considering the pricing of Saatva’s other mattress toppers, $315 for a queen Micro-Coil Mattress Topper seems about right for the brand. The topper is shipped for free and comes with a six-month sleep trial and one-year warrantym which is considered pretty a short warranty period for the luxury topper market.

The Saatva Micro-Coil Mattress Topper has three different layers. The top layer is a cotton cover with Guardin botanical antimicrobial treatment. It prevents the growth of bacteria, mildew, and mold, which is helpful considering the cover is not removeable (and thus not washable).

In the centre of the mattress topper is a one-inch layer of recycled steel micro-coils. They’ve been reinforced along the edges of the topper and in the center third to provide support for your hips and lower back. On either side of the micro-coil layer is gel-infused comfort foam with CertiPUR-US certification for enhanced temperature control.

Four straps are placed on the corners to keep the topper in place. Though I ordered a king topper, it did not fully cover my king-sized mattress, exposing about an inch or two on either side of the topper. (This has been the case for all of the Saatva toppers I've tested, which makes me wonder if my actual mattress is larger than I thought).

Recent findings suggest that my biggest concern about this mattress’ design might be the durability. Foam breaks down faster than natural latex and there is only an inch between your body and the micro coil layer. While I didn’t notice any durability problems during testing, the plusher, soft surface of the topper indicates a softer foam that may not last as long as a firmer foam, especially if you sleep in the same spot night after night.

After a week of testing the Saatva Micro-Coil Mattress Topper, here’s what I can share about the ease of set up, comfort, and temperature regulation.

Recent findings suggest that the Saatva Micro-Coil Mattress Topper arrived vacuum sealed and tightly rolled into a ball. Because of the micro-coils, I had to unfurl the topper by hand and place it in a flat position on my mattress. After putting the straps into place so the topper wouldn’t move, I noticed that it didn’t completely cover my king-size mattress. There was about an inch or two of the mattress visible on either side of the topper.

The topper had a lot of creases and bunching because it appears to have unnecessary, extra fabric. By the time I slept on the topper at night, I could not feel the fabric through my sheets.

The off-gassing of the topper’s foams were noticeable as soon as I removed the packaging, and a week later, I can still smell it.

For a mattress topper with a layer of micro coils, I expected it to be firm and supportive. That’s how Saatva advertises it, but that’s not exactly what I experienced.

Sources indicate that the Micro-Coil Mattress Topper has a plush, soft surface — I rate it as 5/10 on the mattress firmness scale, placing it as medium-plush. My shoulders and hips sunk in enough to allow for deep pressure relief when on my side and felt comfortably supportive when on my back. As a back and stomach sleeper who prefers a firmer mattress feel, the topper was slightly too soft for my preferences. However, the cushioning and cradling nature of the surface would appeal to most sleepers.

In a recent development, stomach sleepers will need something firmer, like the Saatva Graphite Mattress Topper, especially those weighing over 180lbs. Comfort-wise, I’d recommend the Micro-Coil Mattress Topper to those who need to soften a firm mattress.

It has been revealed that thanks largely to its recycled steel coils, the Saatva Micro-Coil Mattress Topper does a decent job with temperature regulation. However, I wouldn’t suggest it for very hot sleepers.

Recent findings suggest that I tested this topper during a particularly cold week in Texas in November when the temperature inside my home was between 64-69 degrees at night. Because it was so cold in the evenings, I’d sometimes fall asleep with a sweatshirt and sweatpants. When that happened, I would wake up slightly warm — but not sweating and not hot. I’d then take off my socks or change into lighter pyjamas and be fine the rest of the night.

In a recent development, the best mattress toppers will provide a comfortable sleep feel, regardless of the temperature of your bedroom. If you like the sound of the Micro-coil, I’d suggest light sleepwear and using breathable sheets.

Whether you overheat easily or not, I’d suggest ordering this topper in the summer and utilize the 180-night sleep trial to make sure it’s a good fit for you.

Sources indicate that rather than separate the topper reviews, Saatva mixed them all together. This means the 4.7 out of 5-star rating from over 305 reviews is a score related to all Saatva’s toppers – and is not accurate for the Saatva Micro-Coil Mattress Topper.

Sources indicate that you can search the topper reviews by keyword and star rating. I typed in “micro coil” and only six reviews popped up. There could be more by other buyers who didn’t mention the term “micro-coil” in their reviews.

Five of the six reviews praised the topper for its soft, contouring feel and how it improved their sleep by making their mattress more comfortable and/or its ability to relieve their pain. One reviewer mentioned returning the micro-coil mattress because it made them very hot at night.

❌ You want a washable, removable cover: You can only spot clean the exterior of this topper as the cover can’t be removed and washed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta employees have expressed concerns about what appear to be major privacy breaches when using Muse, currently the second most popular free iPhone app in the App Store with over 10 million downloads.

This includes again accessing end-to-end encrypted messaging without permission, and sharing what may be the bank balances of another Muse user ….

Siri AI was not the only AI app to launch back in September; Meta’s Muse AI app was introduced the same month, with the firm describing it as “your personal AI agent that gets things done across every part of life.”.

Muse initially launched as an iPhone app, with Mac and iPad apps following shortly afterwards. It immediately moved to the top of the US App Store charts, overtaking ChatGPT. It rapidly exceeded 5 million downloads following a major advertising push by Meta, and that number has since doubled.

It wasn’t long before major privacy concerns were raised. Tech writer Jason Aten reported that the Mac app accessed his messages despite him explicitly refusing permission. The app then lied to him about how it had achieved this. Meta described this as a bug.

Security researcher Patrick Wardle also discovered a zero-day vulnerability that could allow an attacker to hijack dictated prompts, directing them instead to their own server.

I remarked at the time that I would absolutely not be one of the millions of people using the app, and the wisdom of that decision has now been underlined by a fresh report.

Reuters now reports Meta employees discussing further breaches. This includes another example of accessing encrypted messages without permission.

An employee using Muse on her personal phone reported it had surprised her with a reminder to respond to a message from her sister on Signal, an end-to-end encrypted messaging service popular with privacy advocates that competes with Meta’s WhatsApp.

It has been revealed that “This seems like an extreme privacy violation. I definitely did not grant it access to other apps, or recall being asked about this,” the employee stated in her post.

It has been revealed that the report claims this appears to have been done by capturing push notifications. However, this was what the app claimed had happened in the earlier case, and it turned out not to be true. The AI Now Institute was able to replicate the problem of Muse accessing Signal messages without permission.

Another employee reported receiving unsolicited bank balances that they say appeared to be those of another Muse user.

Muse had randomly added an extra message to its regular chats about fishing-related weather and tide information, saying: “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.”.

According to recent reports, “I have never shared my bank account with Muse and never discussed any banking topic with Muse. I’m afraid it’s sending other’s bank info to me,” the staffer wrote in his post.

Meta told Reuters that these were “isolated incidents” and suggested that the bank balances may have been AI hallucinations rather than leaked information. Enhancement: Meta has now told us that the balances were definitely hallucinations.

According to recent reports, "AI Agent" = Malware. There are an expanding number of "I told it not to do that" cases.

It has been revealed that the instructions (prompt) you give the agent are a tiny fraction of the total prompt context the agent uses, and Meta/Grok/etc. is not going to let you see that context. Agents harvesting your data (ex. see full disk access) and sending it to the mothership is just another revenue/training stream. Even if you are paying you are still the product.

Meta has taken concern with the messaging claims. It says that access to either notifications or messaging must be explicitly granted.

In a recent development, with Android, people have the option to grant apps notification access, which allows apps to see notifications as they’re received. This is something users need to opt in to and is not specific to Muse. With Mac, to allow Muse to work on your behalf, you not only need to click allow for accessibility and screen recording, but after that it takes you to a settings screen where you once again need to confirm and turn this on.

The manufacturer also implies that the experience of employees may relate to internal versions of Muse.

Employees have access to different versions of Muse than the public, so they’re often reviewing features, functionality, and behavior not available elsewhere.

I can only repeat my previous take on Muse: Nope.

Patrick Stewart‘s cause of death has been revealed.

The beloved English actor died at age 86 on Oct. 28 in his Los Angeles home. His death was confirmed by a statement on his social media, which added that the cause was “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and lewy body dementia.”.

Sources indicate that his death certificate, obtained by People, lists cardiopulmonary arrest as his cause of death, and neurocognitive disorder with Lewy body as an underlying condition. TMZ was first to report the news.

The Emmy-winning performer, known for both his good natured persona and indelible roles in popular franchises like Star Trek and X-Men, was adored by his collaborators and the public alike. Stewart’s career spanned decades with work across more than five dozen films and over 50 television appearances, from X-Men and Star Trek to Dune and American Dad. His stage roles also ran the gamut from Shakespeare’s Scottish play to Waiting for Godot to his memorable one-man version of A Christmas Carol. In 1966, he joined the Royal Shakespeare Company and he remained with the storied company until 1982. During his tenure at the Royal Shakespeare Company, Stewart featured in numerous productions, including Hamlet, King Lear, and The Taming of the Shrew. He would continue appearing onstage throughout his career, notably joining longtime friend and actor Ian McKellen for Waiting for Godot in 2009 and again in 2014.

In a wave of tributes from Hollywood following his death, William Shatner remembered Stewart, who succeeded him as captain of a Star Trek franchise. “Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor,” wrote Shatner. “From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did.”.

  • Canva today revealed latest controls that will let Free and Pro users choose whether to see generative AI features across the app, as well as how much AI-generated content appears in search results and in recommendations for templates and design elements.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In light of growing pushback from owners who want more control over how AI is integrated into their apps (if at all), Canva is introducing newly introduced settings that let them hide generative AI features and see less AI-generated content. Here are the details.

Canva today revealed latest controls that will let Free and Pro users choose whether to see generative AI features across the app, as well as how much AI-generated content appears in search results and in recommendations for templates and design elements.

The manufacturer notes that both controls are available at no additional cost and can be turned on or off at any time.

According to Canva, “the future of creativity isn’t a choice between AI and no AI.” For this reason, it is introducing the following controls:.

The company says that, while it knows that there is an ongoing debate between consumers with opposing views on whether AI has a place in creative work, it thinks “both views are valid”:.

“It’s not our place to tell anyone how to create, so today we’re launching two upcoming controls that put that decision firmly with our community […].”.

Importantly, the company noted that select features that use AI without generating latest content will remain available even when generative AI features are turned off:.

“Some of Canva’s everyday editing tools use AI to make simple tasks faster, without generating anything new. Background Remover, one of Canva’s most popular tools, lifts a subject cleanly out of a photo in a single click, and Magic Grab lets creators select an object in an image and move it somewhere else in the design. Both remain available when the generative AI switch is off, because they work only with what’s already in a design.”.

Canva added that these tools also won’t add an AI label to a design’s metadata, since that label is reserved for AI-generated content.

As for the firm’s design content library, Canva said that while “a small portion of the library is AI-generated content made by Canva, including some abstract backgrounds and illustrated graphics,” its community has told it “they want an easier way to find design assets made by real people, so the content control reduces the number of AI-generated templates and elements that appear in search results and recommendations.”.

With today’s announcement, Canva is essentially expanding on the AI permissions already available to administrators of Business, Enterprise, Teams, and Education accounts, which let organizations control how their teams use AI.

To learn more about today’s announcement, follow this link.
